newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ICI Australia sees shutdown impact.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ICI Australia sees shutdown impact.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd said on Friday that a six-week shutdown at its Gibson Island nitrogen complex during the year would have an adverse impact on the results for the year to September 30, 1997.

"During the year, the six-week shutdown of the Gibson Island nitrogen complex to upgrade its ammonia capacity will have an adverse efect on the year's results," Managing Director Warren Haynes told the annual meeting.
Despite this, chairman Ben Lochtenberg said the company was on budget for the first two months of the 1996/97 year.
"ICI Australia has set a realistic budget for the 1996/97 year," he told the meeting. "For the first two months of the year, we are tracking reasonably well against this budget."
ICI's chemicals division, which posting pre-abnormal profits of A$96 million in 1995/96, would continue to operate in a difficult environment in 1997, Haynes said.
"The market is highly competitive with strong price pressures from imports, and only slow recovery expected from the building and manufacturing sectors in Australia," he said.
Haynes said the company's explosives unit was expected have continued growth, reflecting export growth in Australian coal and metals to Asian economies.
Only modest growth was expected in the plastics sector during the year during 1997, Haynes said.
"(However) the various restructurings and reorganisation initiatives undertaken during the year should improve the outlook for Plastics in the coming year (1996/97)," he said.
ICI's Plastics profits slumped to A$2 million in 1995/96 from A$73 million in the previous year. Haynes said the outlook for the Advanced Sciences unit was mixed.

While pharmaceuticals was expected to grow strongly and its scientific business would continue expanding in the United States, Haynes forecast subdued growth for the adhesives, resins and polyurethanes businesses.
Lochtenberg said ICI was well advanced in its plans to reduce costs by A$130 million by the end of 1996/97 year.
"We are currently moving the goalposts to increase this target to about A$200 million by 1998," he said.
ICI Australia's net profit for 1995/96 was A$197.1 million, down 26.7 percent. ICI Australia is 62.4 percent owned by Imperial Chemical Industries Plc.
